verified_citation: Gwira JA, Fryar CD, Gu Q. Prevalence of total, diagnosed, and undiagnosed diabetes in adults: United States, August 2021-August 2023. NCHS Data Brief, no 516. Hyattsville, MD: National Center for Health Statistics; November 2024.
study_aim_and_data: NHANES August 2021-August 2023, adults 20+; diagnosed (self-report), undiagnosed (FPG >=126 mg/dL or HbA1c >=6.5% without diagnosis), and total diabetes; trends from 1999-2000.
methods: Taylor series linearization SEs; t tests for pairwise differences; orthogonal contrasts and linear regression for trends; FPG adjusted with NCHS forward regression equations for trends; SAS 9.4 and SUDAAN 11.0; pregnant women excluded.
weight_and_sample_handling: Quote: "Fasting sample weights were used to account for differential probabilities of selection, nonresponse, and noncoverage." Every table note: "Estimates are weighted using fasting sample weights." Unweighted n for August 2021-August 2023 in the trend table is 2,938. HbA1c is used only within the fasting subsample; the phlebotomy weight (WTPH2YR) is not mentioned.
limitation_relevant_here: Reports only the composite (HbA1c or FPG); no HbA1c-only or FPG-only estimates and no HbA1c estimate in the larger phlebotomy sample, so the effect of the fasting-subsample restriction on an HbA1c-based figure is not visible.
overlap_with_this_project: Very high: same cycle, same thresholds, same diagnosed/undiagnosed/total composite; the official benchmark.
what_this_project_adds: Decomposes the official composite into HbA1c-only and FPG-only estimates in one paired domain with a design-based paired difference, and re-estimates HbA1c-defined prevalence in the full phlebotomy domain with WTPH2YR to show how much the sample and weight choice moves it.

verified_citation: Cowie CC, Rust KF, Byrd-Holt DD, Gregg EW, Ford ES, Geiss LS, Bainbridge KE, Fradkin JE. Prevalence of diabetes and high risk for diabetes using A1C criteria in the U.S. population in 1988-2006. Diabetes Care. 2010;33(3):562-568.
study_aim_and_data: NHANES 1988-1994, 1999-2002, 2003-2006 (n = 13,094 in 2003-2006 Table 1); HbA1c-defined diagnosed, undiagnosed, total diabetes and high risk; comparison with FPG and 2-h glucose in the 2005-2006 OGTT subsample (n = 2,017).
methods: Crude and age/sex-standardized prevalence with 95% CIs; concordance of A1C, FPG, and 2-h criteria shown as overlapping categories in the OGTT subsample.
weight_and_sample_handling: Two samples and two weights. HbA1c prevalence: "calculated among examined individuals with known diabetes status based on interview and with valid A1C, using examination sample weights". Definition comparison: "calculated among individuals in the OGTT subsample in 2005–2006, using OGTT sample weights." Figure note: "(n = 2,017); consequently some estimates may differ slightly from those in Table 1."
limitation_relevant_here: Acknowledges that moving HbA1c from its examined sample to the subsample changes estimates but does not quantify or test the difference; predates the 2021-2023 phlebotomy weight; single-measurement definitions.
overlap_with_this_project: High: the clearest located precedent for estimating HbA1c in its own larger sample while comparing definitions in a smaller paired subsample.
what_this_project_adds: A formal, design-based estimate (with uncertainty) of the HbA1c-only prevalence difference between the full phlebotomy domain (WTPH2YR) and the paired fasting domain (WTSAF2YR) for August 2021-August 2023, labelled as a combined selection and weighting comparison.

verified_citation: Hu M, Le MH, Yeo YH, Wijarnpreecha K, Likhitsup A, Kim D, et al. Diabetes prevalence and management patterns in US adults, 2001-2023. Acta Diabetol. 2025;62(12):2159-2170.
study_aim_and_data: NHANES 2001-2002 through 2021-2023, adults 18+ (final n = 27,437); diagnosed and undiagnosed diabetes (FPG >=126 mg/dL or HbA1c >=6.5%), glycemic, BP, and LDL control, medication use; joinpoint trends.
methods: Survey-weighted prevalence with R survey package; Joinpoint for trends; Rao-Scott chi-square and design-based Kruskal-Wallis tests; missingness description in supplementary table.
weight_and_sample_handling: Required both FPG and HbA1c. Quote: "Following the \"least common denominator\" approach recommended by NHANES reporting guidelines" (citations omitted), "fasting subsample weights were used to ensure consistency across analyses". Excluded "missing fasting glucose (n = 31,382)". Missingness check: "Among those with missing fasting glucose levels (n = 31,382), the unweighted prevalence of diabetes was lower than in the overall cohort (11.1% by HBA1C ≥ 6.5% and 12.2% by self-report)".
limitation_relevant_here: The HbA1c comparison for people without FPG is unweighted, pools all cycles, and mixes people never selected for the fasting subsample with fasting-subsample members lacking a valid glucose, so it cannot separate design-based subsampling from nonresponse. Authors note "our estimates may inflate true disease prevalence."
overlap_with_this_project: High: the closest located analysis to this project's sample question and it includes the 2021-2023 cycle.
what_this_project_adds: A weighted, cycle-specific comparison using the documented weight for each laboratory domain (WTPH2YR for HbA1c, WTSAF2YR for fasting glucose and the paired domain), plus a weighted description of who is missing from each domain by age, sex, and race and Hispanic origin.

verified_citation: Davidson MB, Pan D. Epidemiological ramifications of diagnosing diabetes with HbA1c levels. J Diabetes Complications. 2014;28(4):464-469.
accessible_source: Accessed 2026-10-07. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4287398/ (author manuscript; read via NCBI PMC efetch XML)
study_aim_and_data: NHANES 1999-2010, adults 20+ (analytic sample 12,484); total diabetes by history plus FPG-only, HbA1c-only, or either criterion among those without a history; by race/ethnicity, age, BMI, physical activity.
methods: Weighted prevalence by cycle; group differences by chi-square tests (design adjustment not stated); Pearson correlations of prevalence with BMI; SAS 9.1.3.
weight_and_sample_handling: Quote: "Sample \"fasting\" weights, provided by the NCHS, were used to correct for differential selection probabilities and to adjust for non-coverage and non-response." Definitions compared within the fasting sample only.
limitation_relevant_here: Definitional contrast only inside the fasting sample; no estimate of HbA1c in its own larger sample; whether significance tests accounted for the complex design is not verified.
overlap_with_this_project: High on the definition axis (FPG-only versus HbA1c-only total prevalence).
what_this_project_adds: The same definitional contrast for August 2021-August 2023 with a design-based paired difference and CI, plus the second axis (laboratory sample and weight).

verified_citation: Harding JL, Hu C, Varghese JS, Carrillo-Larco RM, Ali MK. Diabetes prevalence, awareness, and control in the United States, 2017-2023. Diabetes Metab. 2025;51(4):101659.
accessible_source: Accessed 2026-10-07. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12162209/ (author manuscript; read via NCBI PMC efetch XML)
study_aim_and_data: NHANES 2017-March 2020 versus August 2021-August 2023; non-pregnant adults 20+; diagnosed, undiagnosed (HbA1c >=6.5% or FPG >=126 mg/dL), total diabetes; awareness; glycemic, BP, lipid control.
methods: Survey-weighted prevalence; Poisson regression with robust SE for pre versus post pandemic prevalence ratios; sensitivity analyses with stricter definitions; SAS 9.4.
weight_and_sample_handling: Participants "had hemoglobin (HbA1c) and fasting plasma glucose (FPG) measures available (n = 3,759 (response rate 46.9%), and 2,938 (response rate = 25.7%) for each period, respectively." Weights: "Sampling weights that were developed by the NCHS to minimize nonresponse bias were used" and "All analyses used recommended sample weights". Weight variable not named (not verified). The 2,938 equals the unweighted 2021-2023 n in NCHS Data Brief 516.
limitation_relevant_here: HbA1c restricted to the paired fasting sample; no HbA1c-only or FPG-only prevalence; weight variable not stated.
overlap_with_this_project: High: same 2021-2023 cycle and composite; has a both-tests sensitivity definition.
what_this_project_adds: Single-biomarker estimates and their paired difference, an explicit weight per domain, and the phlebotomy-domain HbA1c estimate.
